families.COST-CODE: Cost in code and query text
families.COST-CONFIG: Cost in job and compute configuration

stages.commit: On commit, on the developer's machine

gates.block: The change can't merge or deploy until the finding is fixed or accepted in the baseline.
gates.warn: Shown on the pull request, on the changed line. Doesn't stop the merge.
gates.report: Listed in REVIEW.md only. Used for counts, trends and the gap report.

checks.title: Nesting where an early return works
checks.statement: Functions SHOULD return early for simple cases instead of nesting the main path, and SHOULD NOT use an else after a return.
checks.why: A nested version of a discount rule scored 9 for cognitive complexity; the early-return version of the same rule scored 3.
checks.fix: Handle the simple cases first and return; keep the main path flat.

checks.title: Too many arguments
checks.statement: A function SHOULD NOT take more arguments than the threshold in core/gates.yaml; related values SHOULD travel together as one object.
checks.why: A function with nine positional arguments was called with two of them swapped, and no test noticed.
checks.fix: Group related arguments into a small settings object, or split the function.

checks.title: Mutable default argument
checks.statement: A function MUST NOT use a mutable value, such as a list or dictionary, as a default argument.
checks.why: A default list of columns kept growing across calls in the same process, so later batches got extra columns.
checks.fix: Default to nothing and create the value inside the function.

checks.title: Errors caught and hidden
checks.statement: Code MUST NOT catch every error and carry on silently; it MUST catch specific errors and either handle them or re-raise.
checks.why: A broad error catch around a write logged "skipped" and continued; a month of rows was missing before anyone saw it.
checks.fix: Catch the specific error you expect; let everything else fail the job.

checks.title: Commented-out code
checks.statement: The repository SHOULD NOT keep blocks of commented-out code.
checks.why: A commented-out filter was uncommented "temporarily" during an incident and stayed in production.
checks.fix: Delete it; history keeps it.

checks.title: Unused arguments and imports
checks.statement: Functions SHOULD NOT take arguments they don't use, and modules SHOULD NOT import what they don't use.
checks.why: A function kept an unused date argument; callers believed it filtered by date and it didn't.
checks.fix: Remove them.

checks.title: Business thresholds hard-coded in logic
checks.statement: Business values that may change, such as thresholds, rates and lists of codes, SHOULD come from configuration or a named constant, not appear as bare numbers in logic.
checks.why: A fraud threshold of 100 appeared in four places; it was changed in two.
checks.fix: Move it to configuration or one named constant.

checks.title: Logic kept in notebooks
checks.statement: Notebooks SHOULD be thin callers of functions kept in modules, so the logic can be imported, tested and measured.
checks.why: All transforms lived in notebook cells, so there was nothing a unit test could import and coverage read zero.
checks.fix: Move functions into modules; the notebook reads, calls and writes.

checks.title: Public function without type hints
checks.statement: Public functions SHOULD declare the types of their arguments and return value.
checks.why: A transform documented as taking a table name was called with a dataset in one job and a name in another; nothing caught it until run time.
checks.fix: Add type hints; a type checker can then catch the wrong call.

checks.title: Public function without a docstring
checks.statement: Public functions and modules SHOULD have a short docstring that says what they do and what they expect.
checks.why: A shared helper's rounding rule was only discoverable by reading its code, so two teams used it for different purposes.
checks.fix: Add one or two lines saying what goes in, what comes out, and any rule worth knowing.

checks.title: True/false flag argument that switches behaviour
checks.statement: A function SHOULD NOT take a true/false argument that switches between two different behaviours; it SHOULD be two functions or take a named option.
checks.why: A call read load(df, True, False); nobody could tell which flag meant "full reload" without opening the function.
checks.fix: Split into two functions, or use a keyword-only argument with a clear name.

checks.title: A simpler or more modern form is available
checks.statement: Code SHOULD use the simpler equivalent form when one exists, such as a comprehension, any() or all(), a context manager, or newer language syntax.
checks.why: Hand-written loops that built lists and flags made a 20-line function out of what reads as 4 lines in the simpler form.
checks.fix: Apply the automatic fix, then read the result.

checks.title: Function returns a value on some paths and nothing on others
checks.statement: A function that returns a value SHOULD return one on every path, explicitly.
checks.why: A lookup returned a rate on the found path and fell off the end otherwise; a missing rate became a silent empty value in the output.
checks.fix: Return explicitly on every path, or raise when there is no valid answer.

checks.title: Column referenced as an attribute of the dataset
checks.statement: Data-frame code SHOULD refer to columns by name through the column function, not as attributes of a dataset variable, so a transform does not depend on which variable it came from.
checks.why: A transform referred to orders.amount; after a refactor renamed the variable, the reference pointed at the wrong dataset and the join returned the wrong amounts.
checks.fix: Refer to the column by name.

checks.title: Wildcard import that hides built-in names
checks.statement: Code MUST NOT import everything from a module with a wildcard, and MUST NOT shadow built-in names such as sum, max, min or filter.
checks.why: A wildcard import of the engine's column functions replaced the built-in sum; a later line meant to add up a local list called the column function and failed in production.
checks.fix: Import the module under a short alias and call functions through it.

checks.title: Date and time values without a time zone
checks.statement: Code SHOULD create and compare date-time values with an explicit time zone.
checks.why: A job built its run window from local machine time; when it moved to a cluster on UTC, every daily load shifted by five and a half hours.
checks.fix: Use time-zone-aware values, and pass the run date in.

checks.title: Print statements instead of logging, or logging used badly
checks.statement: Production code SHOULD log through the logging library with levels, and SHOULD NOT build log messages eagerly or use print.
checks.why: Prints went to a driver log nobody kept; when a job failed, the only clue had already been lost.
checks.fix: Use a module logger with levels; pass values as arguments to the log call.

checks.title: File paths handled as plain strings
checks.statement: Code MAY use path objects instead of joining strings to build file paths.
checks.why: A path built by string joining lost a separator on one platform and wrote files to the parent folder.
checks.fix: Use path objects.

checks.title: Vague errors, or errors that lose their cause
checks.statement: Code SHOULD raise specific errors with a clear message, and SHOULD keep the original error as the cause when it re-raises.
checks.why: A loader caught a parsing error and raised "load failed"; the file name and line that caused it were lost.
checks.fix: Raise a specific error with the context, chained to the original.

checks.title: Likely bugs
checks.statement: Code MUST NOT contain patterns that are almost always mistakes, such as comparing to itself, a loop variable used after the loop by a closure, or an assertion on a tuple.
checks.why: A late-bound loop variable in a list of functions made every function use the last value; all twelve monthly partitions were written as December.
checks.fix: Fix the pattern the rule names.

checks.title: Test code habits
checks.statement: Test code SHOULD follow the test framework's habits, such as table-driven cases, fixtures for shared setup, and plain assertions.
checks.why: Copied test functions differing in one value drifted apart; a fix to one case never reached the eleven copies.
checks.fix: Turn copies into one table of cases.

checks.title: Local data-frame and array misuse
checks.statement: Code that uses local data frames and arrays SHOULD avoid their known traps, such as chained assignment, in-place changes and deprecated calls.
checks.why: An in-place change on a local copy of query results changed the original too, so a later step saw edited data.
checks.fix: Follow the rule's suggested form.

checks.title: Notebooks chained by running other notebooks
checks.statement: Notebooks SHOULD import shared code from modules instead of running other notebooks to pull in their definitions.
checks.why: A chain of four notebooks that ran each other defined the same helper twice; which one won depended on the order, and tests could not import any of it.
checks.fix: Move shared code into a module and import it.

checks.title: To-do notes left without an owner or ticket
checks.statement: To-do and fix-me notes MAY stay in code only with an owner or a ticket reference.
checks.why: A "TODO handle nulls" note sat in a join for two years until nulls arrived.
checks.fix: Add the ticket, fix it, or delete the note.

checks.title: Very long chains of data-frame calls
checks.statement: Data-frame code SHOULD break long chains of calls into named steps, keeping each chain to the length set in core/gates.yaml.
checks.why: A 30-call chain mixed filters, joins and renames; a reviewer could not see that a filter had moved after a join.
checks.fix: Break the chain into named intermediate steps or small functions.

checks.title: Complex conditions written inline
checks.statement: Complex filter and when-conditions SHOULD be given a name as a variable or function instead of being written inline.
checks.why: An inline condition with six clauses was copied into three places with one clause missing in one.
checks.fix: Name the condition once (for example is_valid_order) and reuse it.

checks.title: Model reads a table directly instead of a declared source or model
checks.statement: Models in a transformation project SHOULD read only declared sources or other models, never a table named directly.
checks.why: A model read a raw table by name; the lineage graph did not show it, so a source change broke the model without warning.
checks.fix: Declare the table as a source and reference it.

checks.title: Model layers skipped or mixed
checks.statement: Models SHOULD follow the project's layers, so that only staging models read sources and later layers read earlier ones.
checks.why: A reporting model joined two raw sources directly; when the staging layer fixed a data issue, the report kept the old error.
checks.fix: Route the model through the staging layer.

checks.title: Empty column added with no type
checks.statement: A column filled with nulls SHOULD be given its data type when it is added, so the table schema does not depend on later rows.
checks.why: A placeholder column added as a typed-less null had no data type; the table write dropped it, and a later union with the typed table failed in production.
checks.fix: Cast the null to the column's type when adding it, for example a null cast to string.

checks.title: Ordered window aggregate with no explicit frame
checks.statement: An aggregate over an ordered window SHOULD state its frame, because ordering silently changes the default frame from the whole partition to a running range.
checks.why: Adding an ordering to a window turned a customer total into a running total; rows with the same date were counted together, and the report was wrong for a month before reconciliation caught it.
checks.fix: State the frame (rows or range, start and end) on every ordered window used by an aggregate; ranking functions need none.

checks.title: Join type left to the default
checks.statement: A join SHOULD state its type, so the reader sees whether unmatched rows are kept or dropped.
checks.why: An inner join written with the default type silently dropped orders whose customer had not arrived yet; a left join was meant.
checks.fix: Pass the join type explicitly, even when it is inner.

checks.title: De-duplication on every column
checks.statement: De-duplication SHOULD name the key columns, so duplicates by key are removed and not only rows that match on every column.
checks.why: A de-duplication on whole rows kept two versions of the same order because a load timestamp differed; revenue was counted twice.
checks.fix: Name the key columns; if whole-row de-duplication is really meant, say so with the allow marker.

checks.title: Whole dataset pulled into one process without a limit
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: Code MUST NOT bring a whole distributed dataset into the single coordinating process, unless a limit or an aggregate makes it small first.
checks.why: A report job converted a full table to a local data frame for a chart. It ran fine on test data and crashed the coordinating process in production after a 40-minute scan.
checks.fix: Aggregate or limit before collecting, or write the result to a table and read that.

checks.title: Engine query or read inside a loop
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: Code SHOULD NOT start a query or a table read inside a loop; it SHOULD express the work as one set-based query.
checks.why: A loop over 300 store ids ran one query per store, each with its own scan and start-up time, and the job took two hours instead of four minutes.
checks.fix: Join or filter on the whole set of keys in one query.

checks.title: Row-by-row loop over collected results
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: Code SHOULD NOT collect rows and then loop over them in the coordinating process to do work the engine can do in parallel.
checks.why: Rows were collected and updated one by one with a call per row; the cluster sat idle while one process did all the work.
checks.fix: Replace the loop with column expressions, a join, or a grouped operation.

checks.title: Row-by-row custom function where a built-in exists
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: Code SHOULD use the engine's built-in functions instead of a row-by-row custom function when a built-in does the same job.
checks.why: A custom function that upper-cased a column made every row cross into a separate interpreter and back, and the step ran ten times slower than the built-in.
checks.fix: Use the built-in function; if none exists, prefer a vectorised (batch) custom function.

checks.title: Columns added one at a time in a loop
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: Code SHOULD add many columns in one projection, not one call per column inside a loop.
checks.why: Adding 200 columns in a loop built a plan 200 levels deep; planning alone took minutes before any data moved.
checks.fix: Build the list of column expressions and add them in one select.

checks.title: Full count used to test for emptiness
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: Code SHOULD test whether a dataset is empty by fetching at most one row, not by counting every row.
checks.why: An "is there anything new?" check counted a billion-row table every hour.
checks.fix: Take one row, or use the engine's emptiness test.

checks.title: Cached data never released, or cached and used once
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: Data cached in memory SHOULD be used more than once and SHOULD be released when no longer needed.
checks.why: Three large intermediate results were cached and never released; later steps spilled to disk and the job ran twice as long.
checks.fix: Cache only what is reused, and release it after the last use.

checks.title: Same table read many times in one job
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: A job SHOULD read each source table once and reuse the result, rather than reading it again in several places.
checks.why: One job read the same orders table in five functions, scanning the same files five times.
checks.fix: Read once in the job's entry point and pass the dataset to the functions that need it.

checks.title: Large output forced into one partition
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: Code SHOULD NOT force a large dataset into a single partition before writing it.
checks.why: A debugging line that merged output into one file was left in; a 200 GB write ran on one core for six hours.
checks.fix: Remove the forced single partition, or apply it only to small outputs.

checks.title: Broadcast inside a loop
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: Code MUST NOT broadcast a dataset to every worker inside a loop.
checks.why: A lookup table was broadcast on every loop pass, sending the same data to every worker hundreds of times.
checks.fix: Broadcast once, before the loop, or join once on the whole set.

checks.title: Debugging actions left in production code
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: Production code SHOULD NOT keep actions added for debugging, such as printing a sample or counting rows, whose results are thrown away.
checks.why: Four leftover row counts each re-ran the whole upstream pipeline, so the job did its work five times.
checks.fix: Remove them, or move them behind a debug flag that is off in production.

checks.title: Schema guessed by reading the data
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: Reads of large or changing sources SHOULD declare the expected schema instead of letting the engine guess it by scanning the data.
checks.why: Schema guessing read every file twice, and one day guessed a column as text instead of a number, which broke the next layer.
checks.fix: Declare the schema, ideally from the data contract.

checks.title: Every column selected from a wide table
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: Queries over wide tables SHOULD name the columns they need instead of selecting all columns.
checks.why: Selecting all 180 columns of a columnar table read every column from storage when the query used six.
checks.fix: List the columns needed.

checks.title: Join with no join condition
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: A query MUST NOT join two tables without a join condition unless the cross product is intended and marked as such.
checks.why: A missing join key matched every order with every customer; the job produced billions of rows and ran until it was killed.
checks.fix: Add the join key. If the cross product is intended, mark it explicitly and keep one side tiny.

checks.title: Function or cast on a partition column in a filter
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: Filters on a partition or clustering column SHOULD compare the column directly, not a function or cast of it, so the engine can skip files.
checks.why: A filter on the year of a date column made the engine read every partition instead of one month's.
checks.fix: Rewrite the filter as a range on the raw column.

checks.title: Merge without a predicate that narrows the target
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: A merge into a large target SHOULD include a condition, such as a date or partition range, that limits which part of the target is scanned.
checks.why: A daily merge of yesterday's changes scanned and rewrote files across three years of the target table.
checks.fix: Add the partition or date range of the incoming changes to the merge condition.

checks.title: Whole result sorted with no limit
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: A query SHOULD NOT sort a whole intermediate result unless the order is used, such as for a limit or a final output.
checks.why: A sort in a view that fed an aggregate forced a full shuffle that changed nothing in the answer.
checks.fix: Remove the sort, or add the limit it was meant for.

checks.title: Union that removes duplicates when duplicates are impossible or wanted
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: A query SHOULD use a union that keeps all rows unless removing duplicates is intended, because removing them needs a full shuffle.
checks.why: Two date ranges that could never overlap were combined with a de-duplicating union, adding a shuffle of the whole result.
checks.fix: Use the keep-all union, and remove duplicates explicitly where they are possible.

checks.title: NOT IN with a subquery
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: A query SHOULD use NOT EXISTS or an anti join instead of NOT IN with a subquery, because one null in the subquery makes the result empty and the plan is often a slow nested loop.
checks.why: A null customer id appeared in the exclusion list and a nightly extract silently returned zero rows.
checks.fix: Rewrite as NOT EXISTS or a left anti join.

checks.title: DELETE or UPDATE with no WHERE
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: A DELETE or UPDATE statement MUST have a condition, unless clearing the whole table is intended and marked as such.
checks.why: A cleanup statement lost its condition in a refactor and emptied a production table.
checks.fix: Add the condition, or replace a full clear with an explicit, marked truncate.

checks.title: Non-repeatable function in a filter
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: A filter SHOULD NOT depend on a function that changes between runs, such as the current time or a random value; the value SHOULD be passed in.
checks.why: A filter on "now minus one day" gave different rows on a rerun, so a backfill could not reproduce the original load.
checks.fix: Pass the run date in as a parameter.

checks.title: Materialized view query blocks incremental refresh
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: The query of a materialized view SHOULD avoid constructs that force a full recompute on every refresh, such as random functions or other non-repeatable functions outside the time filters the platform allows.
checks.why: A random sample in a materialized view's query made every hourly refresh recompute two years of data.
checks.fix: Remove the non-repeatable function, or move it to the query that reads the view.

checks.title: Long chains of materialized views
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: Materialized views SHOULD NOT be stacked deeper than the limit in core/gates.yaml, because each level adds a refresh and a delay.
checks.why: Five materialized views built on each other refreshed in sequence; the top one was always 40 minutes behind its source.
checks.fix: Flatten the chain, or turn intermediate levels into plain views or tables.

checks.title: Columns added by a chain of single-column calls
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: Code SHOULD add several columns in one call or one projection, not a chain of single-column calls.
checks.why: A chain of forty single-column additions made a plan forty levels deep; analysis of the plan took longer than the job's data work.
checks.fix: Add the columns together in one multi-column call or one select.

checks.title: Window ordered over the whole dataset
checks.family_name: Cost in code and query text
checks.statement: A window function SHOULD be partitioned unless the dataset is known to be small, because an ordered window with no partition moves every row into one task.
checks.why: A ranking over all customers with no partition ran in one task on one core while the rest of the cluster sat idle, and spilled to disk once the table grew.
checks.fix: Partition the window by a key; if a global rank is really needed, rank within partitions first or mark the small dataset with the allow marker.

checks.title: Compute with no automatic shutdown
checks.family_name: Cost in job and compute configuration
checks.statement: Every interactive compute definition MUST shut itself down after a set idle time.
checks.why: A shared development cluster with no idle shutdown ran over a long weekend and used a month's budget.
checks.fix: Set an idle shutdown; 30 to 60 minutes is common for development.

checks.title: Scheduled job on shared interactive compute
checks.family_name: Cost in job and compute configuration
checks.statement: A scheduled job MUST run on compute created for the job, not on shared interactive compute that stays on between runs.
checks.why: Nightly jobs pointed at an interactive cluster kept it alive all day and paid the higher interactive price.
checks.fix: Use job compute, created per run and removed after it.

checks.title: No cost tags on jobs and compute
checks.family_name: Cost in job and compute configuration
checks.statement: Every job and compute definition MUST carry tags naming the owning team and the job or product.
checks.why: The bill doubled in one month and nobody could say which project caused it.
checks.fix: Add the tags the platform's cost policy requires.

checks.title: No upper limit on workers
checks.family_name: Cost in job and compute configuration
checks.statement: Autoscaling compute MUST declare a maximum number of workers within the limit the platform policy allows.
checks.why: A skewed join triggered autoscaling to the account maximum; one run cost more than the month's plan.
checks.fix: Set a maximum that fits the job's size and the policy.

checks.title: Always-running pipeline for a batch need
checks.family_name: Cost in job and compute configuration
checks.statement: A pipeline whose consumers need data hourly or less often SHOULD run on a schedule, not continuously.
checks.why: A pipeline set to continuous mode for a daily report kept compute running all day.
checks.fix: Switch to triggered or scheduled runs that match the freshness target.

checks.title: Schedule much more frequent than the freshness target
checks.family_name: Cost in job and compute configuration
checks.statement: A job's schedule SHOULD NOT run more often than its declared freshness target needs.
checks.why: A job feeding a daily dashboard ran every five minutes, so compute never got to switch off.
checks.fix: Align the schedule with the freshness target in the data contract.

checks.title: Oversized compute in development
checks.family_name: Cost in job and compute configuration
checks.statement: Development and test environments SHOULD use smaller compute than production, within a size the policy sets.
checks.why: The development target copied production's 40-worker cluster, so every test run cost as much as a production run.
checks.fix: Override the compute size per environment.

checks.title: Job with no timeout
checks.family_name: Cost in job and compute configuration
checks.statement: Every job SHOULD declare a timeout, so a stuck run stops instead of running until someone notices.
checks.why: A run hung on a locked source for 19 hours with all its workers held.
checks.fix: Set a timeout a little above the job's normal worst run time.

checks.title: Materialized view can't refresh incrementally
checks.family_name: Cost in job and compute configuration
checks.statement: A materialized view over a large source SHOULD be confirmed, before deploy, to be eligible for incremental refresh, or its full recompute SHOULD be recorded as intended.
checks.why: A view was assumed to refresh incrementally; a source format it could not track made every refresh a full recompute for months.
checks.fix: Ask the platform whether the view can refresh incrementally before deploying, and fix the reason it gives.

checks.title: Development views allowed to fall back to full recompute silently
checks.family_name: Cost in job and compute configuration
checks.statement: In development, materialized views meant to refresh incrementally SHOULD use the strict refresh policy, so a view that can't refresh incrementally fails at creation instead of recomputing in silence.
checks.why: The fallback to full recompute was only found in production, when the bill arrived.
checks.fix: Set the strict incremental policy in the development target.

checks.title: Cartesian product in the plan
checks.statement: The physical plan of a job MUST NOT contain a cartesian product unless the job marks it as intended.
checks.why: A join condition referred to the wrong column, so the optimiser dropped it; the query text looked fine but the plan was a cartesian product.
checks.fix: Correct the join condition; the plan check confirms the fix.

checks.title: Nested-loop join
checks.statement: The plan SHOULD NOT use a nested-loop join between two inputs that can be large; the join SHOULD have an equality condition.
checks.why: A join on "date between start and end" became a nested loop that compared every row with every row.
checks.fix: Add an equality key (for example a bucketed date), or turn the range into keys first.

checks.title: Row-by-row custom function evaluation in the plan
checks.statement: The plan SHOULD NOT evaluate row-by-row custom functions on large inputs when a built-in or batch alternative exists.
checks.why: The plan showed every row being shipped to a separate interpreter for a string clean-up a built-in could do.
checks.fix: Replace with built-ins or a batch custom function.

checks.title: Filter not pushed down to the scan
checks.statement: When a query filters a source, the plan SHOULD show the filter pushed to the scan, so files and row groups can be skipped.
checks.why: A filter written after a custom function call could not be pushed down; the job read all files and then threw most rows away.
checks.fix: Filter on raw columns before custom functions and casts.

checks.title: Too many shuffles in one job
checks.statement: A job's plan SHOULD NOT contain more than five data exchanges between workers without a reason recorded in the code.
checks.why: Repeated regrouping by different keys moved the full dataset across the network six times.
checks.fix: Group once by the shared key, or reorder steps so exchanges can be reused.

checks.title: Same source scanned more than once in one plan
checks.statement: A plan SHOULD scan each source once; a repeated scan of the same source SHOULD be replaced by reuse.
checks.why: A self-comparison read the same large table twice in one query.
checks.fix: Read once and reuse, or use a window function instead of a self join.

checks.title: Too many paths through a function
checks.statement: A function SHOULD NOT have more independent paths (cyclomatic complexity) than the threshold in core/gates.yaml.
checks.why: A function with 24 paths needed 24 test cases to cover; it had 3.
checks.fix: Split it into smaller functions, or replace chains of conditions with a lookup table.

checks.title: Function too hard to read
checks.statement: A function SHOULD NOT score above the cognitive complexity threshold in core/gates.yaml; nesting counts extra.
checks.why: Five levels of nested conditions made a pricing rule unreadable, and two reviewers missed a wrong branch.
checks.fix: Return early for simple cases and extract nested blocks into named functions.

checks.title: Function too long
checks.statement: A function SHOULD NOT have more statements than the threshold in core/gates.yaml.
checks.why: A 400-line job function mixed reading, five transforms and writing; nobody could change one step safely.
checks.fix: Extract each step into its own function.

checks.title: Dead code
checks.statement: The repository SHOULD NOT keep functions, classes or modules that nothing uses.
checks.why: An unused copy of an old transform was edited by mistake during an incident instead of the live one.
checks.fix: Delete it; history keeps it.

checks.title: Duplicated logic
checks.statement: The same block of logic SHOULD NOT be copied into several places; it SHOULD live in one function.
checks.why: A tax rule was copied into four jobs; a rate change was applied to three of them.
checks.fix: Move the logic into one shared function and call it.

checks.title: Too many branches or return points
checks.statement: A function SHOULD NOT have more branches or return points than the thresholds in core/gates.yaml.
checks.why: A status-mapping function had 14 return points; a new status fell through to the wrong one.
checks.fix: Replace the branches with a lookup table, or split the function.

checks.title: Query too complex
checks.statement: A query SHOULD stay within the thresholds in core/gates.yaml for joins, nesting depth, conditional branches and common table expressions.
checks.why: A 400-line view with 14 joins and four levels of nested subqueries could not be changed without breaking another report.
checks.fix: Split it into named steps (views or models), each with one job.

checks.title: File too long
checks.statement: A module MAY be split when it grows past the line limit in core/gates.yaml.
checks.why: A 3,000-line utilities file held unrelated helpers; every change to it touched every job.
checks.fix: Split by purpose.

checks.title: Library with a known vulnerability
checks.statement: The project MUST NOT depend on a library version with a known high or critical vulnerability that has a fixed version available.
checks.why: An old HTTP library with a published flaw was pinned for two years because nobody checked.
checks.fix: Upgrade to the fixed version; if none exists, record the risk and a review date in the baseline.

checks.title: Library versions not pinned
checks.statement: Every library the project needs MUST be pinned to an exact version through a lockfile, so every run installs the same versions.
checks.why: An unpinned library released a breaking change overnight and every job that installed fresh failed the next morning.
checks.fix: Generate and commit a lockfile; update it on purpose.

checks.title: Library with a licence the project can't use
checks.statement: The project SHOULD only depend on libraries whose licences are on the organisation's allowed list, and SHOULD flag unknown licences.
checks.why: A library with a licence that barred commercial use was found only during a client's legal review.
checks.fix: Replace the library, or get the licence approved and record it.

checks.title: Unmaintained library
checks.statement: The project SHOULD flag libraries with no release for two years, so a replacement is planned before a flaw appears.
checks.why: A parsing library went unmaintained; when a flaw was published there was no fixed version to move to.
checks.fix: Plan a replacement, or take ownership of a fork.

checks.title: Local test runtime differs from the target runtime
checks.statement: The language and engine versions used for local tests MUST match the versions of the runtime the job is deployed to.
checks.why: Tests passed locally on a newer engine version and the job failed in production on a function the older runtime didn't have.
checks.fix: Pin the test environment to the target runtime's versions, read from the deployment configuration.

checks.title: Libraries installed inside notebooks without versions
checks.statement: Notebooks SHOULD NOT install libraries with in-notebook install commands; when they must, every library SHOULD have an exact version.
checks.why: An in-notebook install without a version pulled a new major release on a Monday and the job broke with no code change.
checks.fix: Declare libraries in the job or environment definition with versions; remove the install command.

checks.title: Every function classified as pure, impure or unknown
checks.statement: The report MUST classify every function as pure, impure (with the reason and line) or unknown, and give the counts per module.
checks.why: Teams asked "how much of our logic is testable?" and nobody could answer without reading every file.
checks.fix: Not a defect; this is the purity report. Use it to choose what to refactor and test first.

checks.title: Logic function does reads or writes that could be passed in
checks.statement: A function that transforms data SHOULD take its inputs as parameters and return its output, leaving table reads and writes to a thin caller.
checks.why: A 300-line function read three tables, transformed them and wrote the result; it could only be tested against real tables, so it wasn't tested.
checks.fix: Split it into a pure transform (data in, data out) and a small caller that reads and writes.

checks.title: Non-repeatable values inside logic
checks.statement: Logic functions SHOULD receive values that change between runs, such as the current time, random values or generated ids, as parameters instead of creating them.
checks.why: A load timestamp created inside the transform made every test result different, so the tests only checked row counts.
checks.fix: Pass the value in; the caller creates it once per run.

checks.title: Logic module imports input and output code
checks.statement: Modules declared as logic SHOULD NOT import modules declared as input and output or platform utilities.
checks.why: A shared helper module imported the platform's utility library, so every test that imported any helper needed a cluster.
checks.fix: Move the platform call to the caller, and declare the module layers in the architecture rule file.

checks.title: Function marked pure that isn't
checks.statement: A function marked as pure MUST NOT be classified as impure by the static check, and MUST NOT touch a table during its unit tests.
checks.why: A function was marked pure years ago; a later change added a lookup read, and its tests quietly began hitting a shared table.
checks.fix: Remove the side effect, or remove the mark.

checks.title: Compute-triggering action inside a logic function
checks.statement: Logic functions SHOULD return a lazy result and leave actions that make the engine run, such as counting or collecting, to the caller.
checks.why: A transform counted its output "for logging", which ran the whole upstream plan an extra time on every call.
checks.fix: Return the result; let the caller decide when to run it.

checks.title: Engine session taken from global scope
checks.statement: Functions SHOULD receive the engine session as a parameter, or not need it, instead of using a global session.
checks.why: Functions used a global session created at import time, so importing a module in a test started a session with the wrong settings.
checks.fix: Pass the session in, or get it from the input data when needed.

checks.title: Query text built from variables
checks.statement: Code MUST NOT build query text by joining strings with variable values; it MUST pass values as query parameters.
checks.why: A table name and a filter value came from a job parameter pasted into the query text; a crafted parameter could read other tables.
checks.fix: Use named query parameters; for identifiers, check the value against an allowed list.

checks.title: Dynamic code execution
checks.statement: Code MUST NOT execute text as code, such as evaluating an expression read from configuration or input.
checks.why: A rule engine evaluated expressions stored in a table; anyone who could write to that table could run code on the cluster.
checks.fix: Parse rules into a small, fixed set of operations, or use a safe expression library.

checks.title: Unsafe deserialisation
checks.statement: Code MUST NOT load serialised objects in a format that can run code, from any source it does not fully control.
checks.why: A model file downloaded from a shared folder was loaded with a format that runs code on load.
checks.fix: Use a data-only format, or verify a signature before loading.

checks.title: Certificate checking turned off
checks.statement: Network calls MUST verify server certificates; code MUST NOT turn verification off.
checks.why: Verification was turned off to get past a proxy error in development and the line shipped to production.
checks.fix: Install the right certificate authority bundle instead.

checks.title: Shell command built from variables
checks.statement: Code MUST NOT run a shell command built from variable text through a shell; it MUST pass arguments as a list.
checks.why: A file name from a landing folder was passed to a shell command; a file named with a semicolon ran a second command.
checks.fix: Call the program directly with an argument list.

checks.title: Secret value written to output or a log
checks.statement: Code MUST NOT print, log or write a secret value read from the secret store.
checks.why: A connection test printed the password it fetched; the job log was readable by the whole workspace.
checks.fix: Log only that the secret was found, never its value.

checks.title: Personal data printed or logged
checks.statement: Code SHOULD NOT print or log samples of columns classified as personal or sensitive.
checks.why: A debugging sample of a customer table, with emails and phone numbers, ended up in job logs kept for a year.
checks.fix: Log counts and column names, not values; mask values if a sample is needed.

checks.title: Broad permission grants in code
checks.statement: Permission grants in code SHOULD go to named groups or service identities with the least privilege needed, never to everyone and never all privileges.
checks.why: A setup script granted all privileges on a schema to all users so a demo would work, and it was never revoked.
checks.fix: Grant specific privileges to a group.

checks.title: Notebook outputs committed
checks.statement: Notebooks MUST be committed without cell outputs, because outputs can hold data samples, personal data or secrets.
checks.why: A notebook was committed with its output cells, including 50 customer rows with emails and phone numbers.
checks.fix: Strip outputs automatically on commit.

checks.title: Other known-unsafe calls
checks.statement: Code SHOULD NOT use calls on the security rule set's known-unsafe list that the checks above don't name, such as weak hashes for security, predictable temporary files, or binding a service to every network interface.
checks.why: A file-integrity check used a weak hash; two different files could be made to look identical.
checks.fix: Use the safe alternative the rule names.

checks.title: Secret in a file
checks.statement: Files in the repository MUST NOT contain secrets such as tokens, keys, passwords or connection strings with credentials.
checks.why: A personal access token in a notebook was pushed to a shared repository and used from outside the company within a day.
checks.fix: Remove it, revoke and rotate the secret, and read it from the secret store.

checks.title: Secret in the repository history
checks.statement: The repository's history MUST NOT contain secrets, even ones removed from current files.
checks.why: A key was deleted from the code in a later commit, but stayed readable in history for anyone who cloned the repository.
checks.fix: Revoke and rotate the secret. Rewriting history is optional once the secret is dead.

checks.title: Credentials in configuration instead of a secret reference
checks.statement: Configuration files MUST refer to secrets by name in the secret store, never hold the secret value.
checks.why: Environment config files held database passwords "just for development", and the production file copied the pattern.
checks.fix: Replace values with secret references resolved at run time.

checks.title: Metric definition doesn't parse or validate
checks.statement: A metric definition MUST match the platform's published specification, and every dimension and measure expression in it MUST parse as valid query text.
checks.why: A typo in a measure expression was found only at deploy time, after the release had already started.
checks.fix: Fix the field or expression the check names.

checks.title: Measure with no aggregate
checks.statement: Every measure MUST aggregate its values, so it gives one answer per group at any level of detail.
checks.why: A measure was written as a plain column; at monthly level it returned one arbitrary row's value instead of the month's total.
checks.fix: Wrap the expression in the intended aggregate.

checks.title: Ratio averaged row by row
checks.statement: A ratio measure MUST be computed as one aggregate divided by another, never as the average of per-row ratios.
checks.why: Margin was defined as the average of each order's margin; small orders counted as much as large ones, and the reported margin was 6 points too high.
checks.fix: Define it as the sum of the numerator divided by the sum of the denominator.

checks.title: Join that can multiply rows, not declared
checks.statement: Every join in a metric definition MUST declare its cardinality, and a join that can match many rows MUST NOT feed a measure that adds up values from the other side.
checks.why: Joining orders to order lines made each order's shipping fee appear once per line, and shipping revenue tripled.
checks.fix: Declare the cardinality; aggregate at the right grain before joining, or measure from the side that is not repeated.

checks.title: Same metric defined differently in two places
checks.statement: A metric name MUST have one definition across the repository; two definitions with the same name and different expressions MUST be reported.
checks.why: Revenue meant gross in one definition and net of refunds in another; two dashboards disagreed by 9% and both were "right".
checks.fix: Keep one definition and reference it; rename the other if it is a different metric.

checks.title: Metric or dimension without a description
checks.statement: Every metric and dimension SHOULD have a description, and metrics SHOULD say what they include and exclude.
checks.why: An assistant answering questions over the metrics picked "orders" instead of "completed orders", because neither was described.
checks.fix: Add descriptions, starting with the most-used metrics.

checks.title: Metric with no test of known answers
checks.statement: Every metric SHOULD have a test that runs its definition on a few known input rows and checks the expected answer at more than one level of detail.
checks.why: A change to a filter in a metric definition passed review and silently dropped cancelled orders from the denominator.
checks.fix: Add input rows and expected answers per metric; the bundle runs them offline.

checks.title: No commit-time checks configured
checks.statement: The repository SHOULD configure the fast checks to run on every commit on the developer's machine.
checks.why: Every problem was first seen in CI twenty minutes after the push, so fixes came in streams of small commits.
checks.fix: Add the commit-time configuration from the bundle's templates.

checks.title: Tests not run on every change
checks.statement: The CI pipeline MUST run the unit tests on every pull request.
checks.why: Tests existed but only ran when someone remembered; three of them had been failing for a month.
checks.fix: Add a test step to the pull-request pipeline and make it a required check.

checks.title: No coverage threshold in CI
checks.statement: The CI pipeline SHOULD fail a change whose changed lines fall below the coverage threshold.
checks.why: Coverage was measured and shown but never enforced; it fell from 70% to 30% in a year.
checks.fix: Add the changed-lines coverage gate.

checks.title: No secret scanning
checks.statement: The repository MUST scan every change, and its history, for secrets.
checks.why: A token sat in the repository for eight months because nothing looked for it.
checks.fix: Add secret scanning to commit-time checks and CI.

checks.title: Main branch not protected
checks.statement: The main branch MUST require a pull request with a review and passing required checks before merge.
checks.why: A direct push to main skipped review and the checks, and broke the nightly load.
checks.fix: Turn on branch protection with required reviews and checks.

checks.title: Deployment configuration not validated before deploy
checks.statement: The deployment configuration MUST be validated, and the configuration cost checks run, before every deploy.
checks.why: A typo in a job definition was found only when the deploy failed halfway, leaving half the jobs on the old version.
checks.fix: Add a validation step before deploy in the release pipeline.

checks.title: Query files not linted
checks.statement: The repository SHOULD lint every query file and query cell, not only the general-purpose code.
checks.why: All the code was linted, but the 40 query files where most of the cost lived were not.
checks.fix: Add the query linter to commit-time checks.

checks.title: No test setup
checks.statement: The repository SHOULD have a test folder, a shared local engine session for tests, and its test libraries declared.
checks.why: The first person to write a test spent a day getting a local session working, so nobody wrote the second test.
checks.fix: Add the test setup from the bundle's templates.

checks.title: Security practices below the agreed score
checks.statement: The repository SHOULD meet the agreed score on a published checklist of security practices.
checks.why: A review found unpinned build actions, no dependency updates and no static analysis, each easy to fix and never noticed.
checks.fix: Fix the lowest-scoring practices first.

checks.title: Models and sources without descriptions
checks.statement: Models, sources and their key columns SHOULD have descriptions, so people and assistants can tell what each one means.
checks.why: Two models named orders_final and orders_clean existed; nobody could say which one the finance report should use.
checks.fix: Add descriptions in the properties files, starting with the most-used models.

checks.title: Code not in the agreed format
checks.statement: Code SHOULD be formatted by the agreed formatter, so changes show only real edits.
checks.why: Pull requests mixed reformatting with logic changes, and a wrong condition hid in 600 lines of whitespace changes.
checks.fix: Run the formatter on commit.

checks.title: Basic lint errors
checks.statement: Code SHOULD pass the basic lint rules for undefined names, unused variables and syntax problems.
checks.why: A misspelt variable name in a rarely used branch failed only when that branch ran in production.
checks.fix: Fix the reported names.

checks.title: Query text not in the agreed format
checks.statement: Query files and query cells SHOULD follow the agreed dialect rules for layout, case, aliases and explicit join types.
checks.why: An implicit join written as a comma between tables hid a missing condition in a long query.
checks.fix: Run the query formatter and fix what it can't.

checks.title: Names that break the convention
checks.statement: Names of functions, variables, classes and tables SHOULD follow the agreed naming convention.
checks.why: Mixed naming styles made the same column appear under three spellings across jobs.
checks.fix: Rename to the convention.

checks.title: Changed lines not covered by tests
checks.statement: The lines a change adds or edits MUST be covered by tests to at least the threshold in core/gates.yaml, counting both sides of every branch.
checks.why: A new branch for "refund" orders was never run by any test and reversed the sign of revenue in production.
checks.fix: Add a test case for each new branch.

checks.title: Pure function with no unit test
checks.statement: Every pure function SHOULD have at least one unit test, because it is the cheapest code to test.
checks.why: The purity report showed 17 pure functions nobody had tested; one of them had a wrong rounding rule for a year.
checks.fix: Add a table of cases (input rows, expected rows) for it.

checks.title: Module with no test file
checks.statement: Every module that holds logic SHOULD have a matching test file.
checks.why: A whole module of business rules had no tests because nobody had created the first test file.
checks.fix: Create the test file with one case; the rest follow more easily.

checks.title: Unit tests need a cluster or network
checks.statement: Unit tests MUST run offline on a developer machine, with a local engine and no network, shared cluster or shared tables.
checks.why: Unit tests ran against a shared workspace; they were slow, failed whenever it was busy, and were eventually skipped.
checks.fix: Use a local session and small in-memory datasets; mock or remove network calls.

checks.title: Tests on pure functions miss deliberate bugs
checks.statement: Tests on pure functions SHOULD catch at least the share of deliberate small code changes set in core/gates.yaml.
checks.why: Coverage was 95%, but changing ">" to ">=" in a discount rule broke nothing in the tests.
checks.fix: Add cases at the boundaries the surviving changes point to.

checks.title: Tests that only check row counts
checks.statement: Tests of data transforms SHOULD compare the actual rows and schema with the expected ones, not only the number of rows.
checks.why: A test checked that 3 rows came out; a bug swapped two columns and the test still passed.
checks.fix: Compare whole datasets, including the schema.

checks.title: Model without data tests
checks.statement: Every model in a transformation project SHOULD have data tests on its key, such as unique and not null, plus any accepted-values rules.
checks.why: A model's key was assumed unique; a source change made it repeat and every downstream total doubled.
checks.fix: Add key tests to the model's properties file.

checks.title: Model logic without unit tests
checks.statement: Models with business logic, such as conditional mappings, date handling or window functions, SHOULD have unit tests with given input rows and expected output rows.
checks.why: A fiscal-week calculation was wrong in the last week of December and only real data ever exercised it.
checks.fix: Add a unit test with rows at the edge cases.

checks.title: Known data pattern without its standard test cases
checks.statement: Code that implements a known data pattern, such as history tracking with versioned rows, de-duplication, incremental loads or late-arriving data, SHOULD be tested against that pattern's standard set of cases.
checks.why: A history-tracking merge was tested only for "new row" and "changed row"; the same batch arriving twice opened a duplicate current version for every customer.
checks.fix: Copy the pattern's case table from the bundle's test kit and run it against your function.
